label: Foundations
notes: Open by positioning this opening chapter as the foundational toolkit for everything that follows in Griffiths-Harris. The deck covers complex differential calculus, sheaves and cohomology, Hermitian and Kahler geometry, vector bundles, divisors, and Hodge theory. The deck follows printed pages 1 through 127. Each later chapter pulls from this toolkit.

label: Complex Calculus
notes: Set up complex calculus. Holomorphic functions satisfy the Cauchy-Riemann equations and the d-bar operator vanishes on them. The Wirtinger operators partial-z and partial-z-bar give a clean way to decompose differentials on complex manifolds. The d-equals-partial-plus-partial-bar decomposition is the workhorse of the rest of the chapter.

label: Sheaves and Cohomology
notes: Introduce sheaves as the bookkeeping for local-to-global data. Sheaf cohomology measures the obstruction to lifting local sections to global ones. The Cech and derived-functor pictures agree under mild hypotheses. The chapter uses sheaf cohomology to manage line bundles, divisors, and holomorphic forms.

label: Hermitian and Kahler
notes: Define Hermitian and Kahler structures. A Hermitian metric on a complex manifold gives a real two-form omega; the Kahler condition is that omega is closed. On a Kahler manifold, Laplacians for d, partial, and partial-bar agree up to constants, which is the engine behind Hodge decomposition.

label: Vector Bundles
notes: Describe holomorphic vector bundles and their cohomology. Line bundles are classified up to isomorphism by their first Chern class in the appropriate cohomology. Higher-rank bundles carry Chern classes that obstruct triviality. The chapter sets up Chern-Weil theory for explicit computations later.

label: Divisors and Linear Systems
notes: Cover divisors. A divisor is a formal sum of codimension-one subvarieties with integer coefficients. Cartier divisors correspond to line bundles. Linear systems are projective parameter spaces of divisors in a given class, and they realize maps from the variety to projective spaces.

label: Hodge Theory
notes: Sketch the Hodge theorem on compact Kahler manifolds. Every cohomology class has a unique harmonic representative, and harmonic forms split by type into the Hodge decomposition. The diamond of Hodge numbers obeys conjugation symmetry and Serre duality. This is the climactic structural result of the foundational chapter.

label: Recap
notes: Close by reviewing the toolkit. Calculus on complex manifolds, sheaves and cohomology, Hermitian and Kahler structures, holomorphic vector bundles, divisors and linear systems, and the Hodge decomposition. Each later chapter relies on this material to produce concrete statements about complex varieties, Riemann surfaces, and complex surfaces.
